premises.statement: The local planning domain is this finite curb-to-curb pavement patch, including the current ego footprint and proposed braking route. Within this patch adopt no new unobserved entrant during [0,2]. Distant curbside rows remain parked outside the patch, the distant forward white car does not reverse into it, and rear-intersection traffic does not reach it. This premise supports the local task and entrant exclusion only: it does not support or spatially restrict any retained actor BODY estimate, alignment, scenario or occupancy source. All nine declared obstacles remain in the scene with their full sources even where those extend outside this patch. Their movement conditions and geometry are independently defined by the unrestricted common and actor-specific premises. These domain exclusions are falsifiable conditions, not claims that the surrounding world has no other traffic.

Assume the individually observed right parked sedan is approximately 4.8 m long and 1.85 m wide. Its apparent rear width, side foreshortening, pavement contact region and perspective relative to the black SUV support approximate metric depths and lateral offsets. Intrinsics/extrinsics establish viewing directions, not certified monocular depth. Front and oblique views support an approximately straight 14.5 m curb-to-curb paved segment: right curb near y=-6.2 and opposite curb/junction edge near y=8.4. The convex road polygon truncates this observed continuous pavement longitudinally; its rear portion is supported by side views and recent forward views. Parking pavement is included but its obstacles are not removed. Native dimensions, positions, yaw angles and residuals are model estimates. This common premise applies to the complete retained actor bodies and sources without spatial restriction, including bodies beyond the local planning patch.

The black SUV is visibly oriented across the left portion of the road toward ego's side. Retain a slow/yielding mode with decreasing-y displacement of 0-4 m and absolute x displacement at most 0.2 m, and a reasonable adverse continuing mode with decreasing-y displacement of 0-8 m and absolute x displacement at most 0.4 m. Motion is continuous; ground speed is no greater than 4 m/s. Heading remains within 0.03 rad of native yaw -1.48. Source rectangles enclose the full rotated body over all these intermediate poses. No reversal or larger longitudinal excursion is included. These are complete retained modes within these adopted movement conditions, not an exhaustive claim about possible driving.

Center y remains within 0.1 m of 4.5 in the adopted mode and within 0.3 m in the adverse mode. Yaw remains within 0.02 rad of 3.1. Source rectangles include complete bodies for every intermediate pose. No turn across the centerline is adopted. The inventory covers the stated bounded approach conditions.

The front-left image shows the silver SUV behind the black SUV at the side-street mouth. From its actual capture offset -0.005867 s through reference and the two-second horizon, adopt ground speed no greater than 2 m/s. This low-speed condition is an explicit model assumption for both past alignment and future modes. Its evidence center [7.5,11.01] differs from the reference center by 0.01 m, within the 0.012 m alignment bound. The waiting mode keeps the reference heading and permits at most 0.05 m translation. The adverse creeping mode permits decreasing-y displacement of 0-4 m after reference, absolute x displacement at most 0.2 m and yaw within 0.03 rad of -1.5. Source rectangles include full bodies throughout. These waiting/creeping modes cover the adopted conditions.

Observed people are on sidewalks, not presently crossing the ego route. Adopt continuous sidewalk-only motion with ground speed at most 1.5 m/s, including the actual asynchronous capture ages through time zero. This explicitly assumed walking-speed bound supports both retained modes during alignment: the right man's evidence age is 0.041922 s and evidence-to-reference center displacement is 0.04 m; the left pair's evidence age is 0.005867 s and their estimated centers are unchanged. Adopted right-side modes permit absolute x displacement at most 2 m and center y variation at most 0.1 m. Adopted left-side modes wait with absolute displacement along either axis at most 0.1 m. Adverse modes permit absolute x displacement at most 3 m and curbward motion, subject to the walking-speed bound. These bands include the initial bodies. Arbitrary pedestrian yaw is enclosed by the source rectangles with outward room for the rotated native square bodies. Running or walking into the roadway is explicitly excluded, not ruled out by observation. The adopted and adverse sources cover all retained sidewalk movement conditions.

anchors.rationale: The individually visible curbside silver sedan has ordinary midsize-sedan proportions. The 4.8 m conditional length prior equals its native body length; it is not a measured dimension.
The visible rear and oblique side support an ordinary sedan-width prior of 1.85 m, exactly matching its native width hypothesis rather than claiming known ground truth.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: In the reference front image the right sedan's rear is several hundred pixels wide and its side recedes toward the vanishing direction. Approximately 1253-pixel focal length together with the 1.85 m width prior suggests rear depth of order ten metres; accounting for the 4.8 m longitudinal body gives an approximate center near x=12 m. The rightward viewing bearing motivates center y=-4.4 m. The black SUV's approximately 4.7 m cross-road length and roughly 500-pixel horizontal extent independently suggest a low-teens longitudinal distance. These conditional body-size anchors, visible pavement perspective, lane markings and oblique curb observations motivate the native local road and actor estimates. Camera calibration supplies axes and rays, not certified depth or ground contact. Nonzero road uncertainty and total actor residuals remain uncalibrated model estimates.
